# GoogleSQL compliance: multi_level_emps_metrics_by_dept in multi_level_aggregation_basic.test.
# The repeated employee rows represent the LEFT JOIN to dependents. Employees 4 and 6 earn the
# same salary but are different employees. COUNT(*) still counts at the joined row grain.
WITH employees AS (
  SELECT * FROM UNNEST([
    STRUCT(1 AS id, 101 AS dept, 200000 AS salary, 45 AS age, 1 AS copies),
    (2, 102, 180000, 42, 3), (3, 101, 150000, 28, 2), (4, 102, 80000, 25, 1),
    (5, 101, 70000, 29, 1), (6, 102, 80000, 37, 1)])
), metrics AS (
  SELECT dept, SUM(ANY_VALUE(salary) GROUP BY id) AS total,
    ARRAY_AGG(ANY_VALUE(age) GROUP BY id ORDER BY ANY_VALUE(age)) AS ages,
    COUNT(*) AS joined_rows
  FROM employees CROSS JOIN UNNEST(GENERATE_ARRAY(1, copies))
  GROUP BY dept
)
SELECT TO_JSON_STRING(ARRAY(SELECT AS STRUCT * FROM metrics ORDER BY dept));
=> "[{\"dept\":101,\"total\":420000,\"ages\":[28,29,45],\"joined_rows\":4},{\"dept\":102,\"total\":340000,\"ages\":[25,37,42],\"joined_rows\":5}]"

# GROUP BY produces no inner groups on empty input; COUNT on those groups returns zero.
SELECT COUNT(MAX(n) GROUP BY n) FROM UNNEST(ARRAY<INT64>[]) AS n
=> "0"
